context.description: Two siblings with no order between them become ready in the same step

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-RM16.spec.ts (3 tests, 24 expect calls; my bun run: 3 pass, 0 fail, 42.6 s under load average about 130-150). The test drives the real code: a spec folder written to a scoped temporary directory and loaded by the real Blend.load (failures asserted empty) and TaskCommand.plan; facts folded through TaskEngineXState.apply; readiness read from the work-region state, the <id>:ready tag, TaskEngineXState.waitingOn, TaskStatus.project and RunSupervisor.supervised. No mocks. GIVEN leaves T1.1, T1.2 after T1.1, T1.3 after T1.1: test 1 asserts the loaded plan (T1 parent required by rule R2; T1.1 no after; T1.2 and T1.3 each after [T1.1] only, so no order between them) and that at start only T1.1 is ready and supervised while both siblings wait on T1.1. WHEN the fact that makes T1.1 trusted is applied: test 2 folds T1.1 to verifying (asserted), both siblings still waiting on T1.1 and unsupervised, then calls engine.apply once with task.verified carrying the trust of T1.1.c1 and asserts T1.1 trusted in that returned snapshot. THEN both ready in that snapshot: on the same returned snapshot T1.2 and T1.3 each equal READY (machine ready, ready tag, waitingOn []), and RunSupervisor.supervised names exactly T1.2 and T1.3; the log entries of that one step are only T1.1.c1 and T1.1 to trusted, so neither sibling is ordered first. Test 3 repeats the check on the other path to trusted (passed results, task.verified with no verdict) and shows one sibling building leaves the other ready. Every Gherkin step has specific assertions on the single apply result.
